paragraphs.text: Markdown in DeepSeek Harness: sent user messages render as Markdown and the composer shows a live re
ndered preview with in-place syntax highlighting.
# dsh-better-markdown
**Markdown where you actually use it: the composer and your own messages.**

DeepSeek Harness renders assistant replies as Markdown, but the composer is a
plain-text editor and

sent user messages come back as plain text. This plugin
closes that gap:

- **Live preview above the composer.** Type Markdown and the rendered result
appears immediately — h

eadings, bold/italic, inline code, lists, task lists,
quotes, tables, fenced code with syntax highli

ghting, links, footnotes and
math, all through DSH's own Markdown pipeline.
- **In-place syntax high

lighting.** The composer itself dims `#`, `**`, `` ` ``
and list markers, and paints emphasis, code,

links and headings, so you can
read the structure while typing. The draft text never changes.
- **U

ser messages render as Markdown.** Every sent message you wrote with
Markdown shows as Markdown in t

he transcript — while the copy action, the
session log, and the text the model sees stay byte-identi

cal.
- **One switch, remembered per browser.** The `M↓` button in the composer
toolbar toggles the p

review (`⌘⇧M` / `Ctrl+Shift+M` also works);
the choice survives reloads. The transcript rendering fo

llows the plugin
configuration, not the button.
Live rendered preview above the composer; the raw draft keeps its Markdown markers, dimmed.
> Third-party plugin. Not an official DeepSeek / DeepSeek Harness component.
## Install

This plugin is distributed **only through GitHub** — it is not published on
npm. Requirements: **DSH

0.2.1-rc.5 or newer, below 0.3.0**, with the Web or
Desktop surface, and Node ≥ 22.

The same spec works in **Plugins → Add** in the app. A version tag pins a
release (`github:ceasarXuu

/dsh-better-markdown#v0.1.0`), and a GitHub Release
tarball can be installed instead when your netwo

rk setup prefers plain
artifacts:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Manual profile row (after the package is installed into the profile):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Disable the bundle and the shipped plain-text behavior returns immediately.
## Switches

All switches are plain booleans on the plugin row; the browser reads them from
`GET /plugin/better-m
arkdown/config` on page load.
| Switch | Default | What it does |
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch for every surface. Off restores shipped behavior while the plug

in stays installed. |
| `transcript` | `true` | Render sent user messages as Markdown in the convers

ation. |
| `composer` | `true` | Enable the composer preview and its toolbar switch. |
| `syntax` |

`true` | Paint Markdown syntax inside the composer (CSS Custom Highlight API). |
| `preview` | `true
` | Show the preview by default when the draft contains Markdown. |

The toolbar switch is the per-browser override: pressing it off turns the
preview off on this browse

r only (`localStorage` key
`better-markdown.prefs.v1`); pressing it on shows the preview for any
non
-empty draft. Clearing site data returns to the host default.
## How it works

Everything runs in the browser half; the host half only publishes the
switches, so there is no netwo
rk traffic beyond the same-origin config read.

- **Transcript.** DSH parses user text into runs and reference chips and
renders each run through th

e keyed `conversation.user.text.node` slot. This
plugin registers the `text` key at a lower priority

than the shipped cell and
renders the run with the platform's own `MarkdownText` component. Session

`@`-mention chips keep their shipped renderer, and copy/quote behavior keeps
reading the original t

ext.
- **Preview.** A normal `conversation.input.dock` entry (the same flow the
shipped queue and to

do docks use) reads the live draft and renders it with
the same `MarkdownText` component.
- **In-pla

ce highlighting.** A `conversation.input.right` cell provides the
switch, and a small controller rep

aints `CSS.highlights` over the composer's
text nodes. Highlights only change paint (color, backgrou

nd, underline,
text-shadow) — never layout, never the draft, never IME composition.

Because rendering uses `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` from the
platform module table, user

messages get exactly the GFM renderer assistant
replies use: sanitized links, highlighted code, tabl

es, footnotes and math.
If that module is unavailable the plugin degrades to plain text instead of
b

math.
If that module is unavailable the plugin degrades to plain text instead of
breaking the page.
### Markdown in a chat message

- Single newlines stay line breaks: outside code blocks, tables and indented
blocks, a newline becom

es a CommonMark hard break before rendering, so a
multi-line message does not collapse into one para

graph.
- Plain prose stays byte-identical to the shipped bubble; Markdown rendering
only starts when

the message contains Markdown syntax (`#`, fences, lists,
quotes, tables, emphasis, code, links, ta

sk items).
- The queue dock's one-line preview renders the same content inline, clamped to
a single

line.
- The **session title**, sidebar rows and headers are host-generated plain text
and are intent

on title**, sidebar rows and headers are host-generated plain text
and are intentionally left alone.
## Limitations

- DSH's composer is a shell-owned Lexical editor. A plugin can decorate it but
cannot turn it into a

WYSIWYG surface, so "Markdown in the composer" means a
rendered preview plus paint-only syntax high

lighting — editing, caret, undo
and Chinese IME all stay with the shipped editor.
- Highlighting nee

ds the CSS Custom Highlight API (Chromium 105+). On a
browser without it the plugin simply skips tha

t layer; the preview and the
transcript keep working.
- The transcript renderer targets DSH 0.2.x sl

ot contracts. A future change to
`conversation.user.text.node` or `conversation.input.dock` needs a

plugin
update; the plugin never patches DSH source.
